questions.stem: For infective endocarditis prophylaxis, what two things must both be present?
questions.answer: A high-risk patient and a high-risk procedure

questions.stem: For infective endocarditis prophylaxis, which procedure type alone is an indication?
questions.answer: Dental procedures

questions.stem: How many high-risk patient groups are defined for infective endocarditis prophylaxis?
Fully repaired congenital heart disease is high risk for endocarditis prophylaxis if repaired within ____.
questions.answer: 6 months

questions.stem: What is infective endocarditis?
questions.answer: Infective inflammation of the endocardium and valves

questions.stem: Which heart valve does infective endocarditis most often affect today?
questions.answer: Aortic valve

questions.stem: Where does the pathogenesis of infective endocarditis start?
questions.answer: At a site of endothelial damage

questions.stem: In infective endocarditis, what role does the sterile thrombotic vegetation play?
questions.answer: Lets bacteria stick during transient bacteraemia

questions.stem: In infective endocarditis, what does platelet and fibrin deposition set up?
questions.answer: A positive feedback cycle

questions.stem: In infective endocarditis, what proportion of cases affect the right side of the heart?
In right-sided infective endocarditis, what is the usual cause?
questions.answer: IV drug use

questions.stem: In right-sided infective endocarditis, which valve is involved in 98% of cases?
In infective endocarditis of a prosthetic valve, what time window defines early?
In prosthetic valve endocarditis, 'late' means onset beyond ____.
questions.answer: 1 year

questions.stem: Which combination of Duke criteria findings meets the threshold for infective endocarditis?
options: 3 major, or 2 major plus 3 minor, or 1 minor
2 major, or 1 major plus 3 minor, or 5 minor
2 minor, or 1 major plus 2 minor, or 4 minor

questions.stem: In the Duke criteria for infective endocarditis, above what temperature is fever counted?
How can the clinical severity of infective endocarditis range?
questions.answer: From no symptoms, through malaise, night sweats, anaemia and weight loss, to cardiogenic shock and sepsis

questions.stem: What proportion of infective endocarditis occurs on normal valves?
What examination findings can infective endocarditis produce?
questions.answer: Murmurs, heart failure, valve lesions, stroke, splenomegaly

questions.stem: Which peripheral stigmata can infective endocarditis cause?
questions.answer: Clubbing, splinter haemorrhages, Osler's nodes, vasculitic rash, retinal changes

questions.stem: Where can emboli from infective endocarditis lodge?
questions.answer: Brain, lungs, limbs, organs

questions.stem: In infective endocarditis, in what proportion of cases are blood cultures positive?
How many blood culture sets from different sites are ideally taken in suspected infective endocarditis?
Which organism causes about half of infective endocarditis cases?
Strep viridans causes about what share of infective endocarditis cases?
Which Gram stain group causes most infective endocarditis?
questions.answer: Gram-positive

questions.stem: Which ECG changes can infective endocarditis cause?
questions.answer: PR prolongation, P mitrale, T wave inversion

questions.stem: What is the sensitivity of transthoracic echo for infective endocarditis?
What is the sensitivity of transoesophageal echo for infective endocarditis?
When is transoesophageal echo mandatory in infective endocarditis?
questions.answer: If paravalvular complications are suspected, e.g. in a shocked patient

questions.stem: On echo, above what vegetation size in infective endocarditis is embolic risk higher?
Which echo finding does TTE detect especially poorly in infective endocarditis?
questions.answer: Peri-annular abscess

questions.stem: On echo, what finding in a prosthetic valve suggests infective endocarditis?
questions.answer: New prosthetic valve dehiscence

questions.stem: How long is IV antibiotic treatment given for infective endocarditis?
In older AHA advice, which procedures needed prophylaxis for valvular disease, including rheumatic?
questions.answer: Dental, GI or GU procedures

questions.stem: Why does current guidance restrict infective endocarditis prophylaxis for most procedures?
questions.answer: Antibiotic harms outweigh the IE risk from most procedures

questions.stem: Which year does the current infective endocarditis prophylaxis guideline date from?
How should infective endocarditis prophylaxis antibiotics be timed relative to a high-risk procedure?
options: Single dose before the procedure, or within 2 hours of it
Single dose after the procedure, for 2 days
Daily doses for 7 days before the procedure

questions.stem: Which oral antibiotic is the first choice for infective endocarditis prophylaxis?
Which infective endocarditis prophylaxis antibiotic is given at 50mg/kg IV or IM?
Which infective endocarditis prophylaxis antibiotic at 50mg/kg PO is used in penicillin allergy?
What should be done for an active infection at the operative site with a likely IE-causing organism?
questions.answer: Give perioperative treatment and ask infectious diseases
